tiers.name: global
tiers.holds: Values: the grey and brand ramps, font sizes and families, spacing, radii, stroke widths, durations, curves and the shadow ramp.
tiers.readByComponents: Yes, for everything but colour: a component reads its sizes, spacing, radius and motion from global tokens.

tiers.name: alias
tiers.holds: Colour roles over the globals: color{Family}{Role}{Level}{State}. The only tier a component reads colour from.

themes.text: The default: web brand ramp, light.
Windows high contrast: the eight system colours only (see highContrast).
The Teams brand ramp; differs from value only where brand enters.

naming.text: A colour token reads color, family, role, level, state: colorNeutralBackground1Hover is the neutral family, background role, level 1, hover state. A token with no state suffix is the rest value.

rules.text: There are no component tokens. A component's styles file hard-codes its sizes, spacing choices and which alias tokens it reads; a spec carries those numbers in values and cites the file.
Interaction states are separate tokens, not layers over the rest colour: hover reads colorNeutralBackground1Hover, pressed colorNeutralBackground1Pressed. Never derive a state colour by blending.
Theme by replacing alias values; the resolved file gives each theme's value under its key. A brand theme replaces the brand ramp, which the alias file reads as brand[10..160].
In fluent.resolved.json a token is {tier, type, value, dark?, highContrast?, teamsLight?, teamsDark?, alias?}; a theme key appears only where that theme differs from value.

units.dimension: px, at 1x; scale by the display's device pixel ratio.
units.cubicBezier: [x1, y1, x2, y2] control points of a CSS cubic-bezier.
units.color: #rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa where the source keeps an alpha colour; the source's rgba() and transparent are normalised to that.
units.shadow: Layers of {x, y, blur, color}, ambient first, no spread; paint every layer.
units.typography: {fontFamily token name, fontSize px, fontWeight, lineHeight px}; no letter spacing.

families.name: neutral
families.text: Greys for surfaces, text and strokes. Foreground 1 is primary text, 2 secondary, 3 tertiary, 4 placeholder-weight; Background 1 is the top surface, 2 to 6 step down behind it.

families.name: brand
families.text: The accent: brand backgrounds for primary actions with colorNeutralForegroundOnBrand on them, brand foregrounds for links and selected marks, brand strokes for selection.

families.name: subtle
families.text: Transparent at rest, a neutral tint on hover and press: the family for subtle buttons and menu items.

families.name: transparent
families.text: Explicitly nothing, for a stroke or background a component must set but not show.

families.name: status
families.text: Success, warning and danger, each with a background, a foreground and a border, mapped onto the green, orange and cranberry palettes.

families.name: palette
families.text: Named colours for badges, avatars and presence, each with Background 1 to 3, Foreground 1 to 3, Border. Not for chrome.

color.pairing: A foreground pairs with a background of the same family and level: colorNeutralForeground1 on colorNeutralBackground1, colorNeutralForegroundOnBrand on colorBrandBackground, colorStatusDangerForeground1 on colorStatusDangerBackground1. A level-2 foreground on a level-1 background is secondary text, still a valid pair.
color.levels: Background levels are depth, 1 nearest the reader: cards and inputs sit on 1, the page on 2 or 3, recessed wells on 4 to 6. In dark themes the order is the same; the greys invert.

strokes.text: Stroke 1 is a control's resting border, 2 a lighter divider, 3 the lightest; StrokeAccessible passes 3:1 against Background 1 for controls that must be findable by their border alone (checkbox, radio, switch off).

brand.text: Every brand alias resolves to one step of a 16-step ramp, brand 10 darkest to 160 lightest. Web light reads brand 80 as colorBrandBackground and brand 70 hover; dark reads 70 and 80. Teams supplies its own ramp; the alias mapping is the same.

status.text: statusColorMapping.ts binds each status to a shared palette; the status aliases copy that palette's tokens. A component may read a palette token directly instead: the progress bar's error is colorPaletteRedBackground3 and its warning colorPaletteDarkOrangeBackground3, not the status aliases.

shadowColors.text: Shadows are two layers, ambient then key, in the neutral shadow colours; brand-coloured surfaces use the brand pair through the shadow*Brand tokens.

ramp.text: Eleven sizes from caption2 to display, each a fixed size and line height; the Strong and Stronger twins keep both and raise the weight to semibold and bold.
ramp.controlLabel: Buttons and inputs set fontSizeBase300 with fontWeightSemibold (button) or fontWeightRegular (input) and lineHeightBase300 directly, not a named style.

weights.text: Semibold is the emphasis weight: button labels, strong styles, selected tabs. Medium is rarely read.

fontFamilies.text: Segoe UI first, then the platform sans; Consolas for code; Bahnschrift for tabular numerals.

standIn.text: Segoe UI is proprietary. Selawik, Microsoft's open Segoe-metric family under the SIL Open Font License, has the same widths and vertical metrics and is the honest stand-in where Segoe is absent; the ramp's line heights assume it.

rules.text: Text sits in a line box of the style's lineHeight; centre the font's ascent plus descent in it.
There are no letter-spacing tokens; draw at the font's natural tracking.

scale.text: Uniform corner radii; no per-corner tokens. A component that rounds corners unequally (a split button's inner edge, a tab's indicator) says so in its spec.

rules.text: Controls (button, input, checkbox, menu, tooltip) use borderRadiusMedium; a rounded button reads borderRadiusLarge for large size, borderRadiusSmall for small; circular is borderRadiusCircular, 10000px, meaning a pill or a circle.
Surfaces (card, dialog) use borderRadiusMedium to borderRadiusXLarge; the spec says which.
The focus outline follows the component's radius, never larger.

scale.text: One scale in two axes, so a horizontal and a vertical token can differ per theme: none 0, XXS 2, XS 4, SNudge 6, S 8, MNudge 10, M 12, L 16, XL 20, XXL 24, XXXL 32.

rules.text: Horizontal padding inside controls comes from the horizontal tokens; vertical padding is often a hard-coded pixel value chosen to hit the control height, and the spec gives it in values.
Gaps between an icon and its label use spacingHorizontalSNudge (6px) at medium size, XS at small, SNudge at large.

tokens.text: Six shadow tokens named by their key blur: shadow2, 4, 8, 16, 28, 64, each two layers, ambient (0 0 2px or 0 0 8px) then key (offset downward by half the blur). The Brand twins carry brand-tinted shadows for brand surfaces.

uses: secondary, outline and every button appearance when focused (composed into the focus style)
avatar's active shadow at 120px and up

rules.text: Depth is carried by shadow and by background level together: a popover is shadow16 on colorNeutralBackground1 over a page on Background 2 or 3.
Under forced colours shadows vanish; every floating surface must also have a visible border there (see highContrast).

states.text: A control paints its rest, hover, pressed and selected looks from four separate tokens per property (background, foreground, stroke). Pressed wins over hover; selected combines with hover and pressed through the SelectedHover-style tokens where they exist, else keeps its selected colour.

disabled.text: Disabled swaps every colour for the Disabled token of its role and takes no input; nothing is dimmed by opacity. Backgrounds go to colorNeutralBackgroundDisabled, text and icons to colorNeutralForegroundDisabled, borders to colorNeutralStrokeDisabled; a transparent or subtle control keeps its transparent background.
disabled.highContrast: Under forced colours disabled text and borders are the system GrayText.

focus.text: Keyboard focus only: the indicator appears when tabster marks the element focus-visible, never after a pointer press. The default indicator is an outline drawn just outside the element by a pseudo-element: 2px solid colorStrokeFocus2 following borderRadiusMedium, its outer edge 2px beyond the element. Buttons draw it inside instead: a 1px colorStrokeFocus2 ring inset from the edge plus the border turned colorStrokeFocus2, so packed controls do not overlap rings. colorStrokeFocus1 (white on light) is the inner contrast ring where a component draws both.
focus.highContrast: Under forced colours the outline is the system Highlight colour.

selection.text: A selected control shows it by colour, not by a layer: checked checkboxes fill colorCompoundBrandBackground, selected tabs draw a colorCompoundBrandStroke indicator, subtle selected items read colorSubtleBackgroundSelected.

targetSize.text: Fluent draws no invisible touch target: the hit area is the visual. Medium controls are 32px tall, small 24, large 40; a 16px checkbox or radio box sits in a 32px row that is the target.

durations.text: 50 to 500ms. Colour transitions on controls use durationFaster; surfaces entering use durationNormal; a switch thumb durationNormal; a spinner loop durationUltraSlow times three.

curves.text: easyEase for colour and small moves; decelerate for entering, accelerate for leaving; linear for loops.

rules.text: A control transitions background, border and color together over durationFaster with curveEasyEase; nothing else animates on hover or press.
There are no springs. Every animation is a duration and a curve.

reducedMotion.text: When the user prefers reduced motion, transitions run in 0.01ms: the end state appears at once.

controlHeights.text: Every control comes in the three sizes; medium is the default. Widths are content plus padding, with a minimum on buttons (96px medium, 64 small).

grid.text: Sizes and spacing fall on a 4px grid, with the SNudge and MNudge tokens off it for optical balance.

layout.rtl: Mirror horizontal padding, icon order and directional icons under right-to-left; the tokens themselves are direction-free.

highContrast.text: The teamsHighContrastTheme binds every colour alias to one of the eight Windows system colours, and the styles files add forced-colors rules that read the CSS system colour names directly. A renderer without CSS reproduces both: bind the highContrast theme, and apply these rules. A styles file may also name a CSS system colour the theme does not bind (ButtonBorder); the list says what to map it to.

systemColors.name: Highlight
systemColors.use: hover and selected backgrounds, focus outlines, selected strokes

systemColors.name: ButtonBorder
systemColors.use: an unchecked radio's border; a CSS system colour the styles name that the high-contrast theme does not bind, so a renderer maps it to ButtonText

rules.text: Hover and press invert: background Highlight, text and border HighlightText, or the reverse as the spec says; forcedColorAdjust none keeps the swap.
Disabled reads GrayText for text and borders.
Every surface that floated by shadow gets a CanvasText border, since shadows do not render.

provenance.text: All facts derive from Fluent UI React v9 at one commit of microsoft/fluentui and the @fluentui/tokens package that commit publishes.
provenance.values: tokens/fluent.resolved.json holds the values the published package gives each theme (tools/tokens.mjs reads upstream/npm/package), so they are what an app gets, not a re-derivation.
provenance.aliases: The alias field comes from the generated alias files in upstream/tokens/alias, read for the global each light value names; 164 of 366 alias tokens name one, the rest are computed in code.
provenance.sources: Component behaviour is read from each component's styles and types files in upstream/components; the Fluent 2 design site fills anatomy and usage where the code is silent, cited as fluent2:<page>.
